notes:

The replication liking d = 1.08 is paired with the t test p < .001, not the separate chi-square p = .001. Analytic letter-level n was not explicitly printed, so n is null.
Source follow-up: Unassigned side not examined. Primary PDF5,10,12 rendered and verified. Printed descriptive probabilities are0.20 versus0.30, reported as50 per cent more likely; no conversion performed. Combined p concerns same full first-and-family-name contrast. Table2 prints0.0001; canonical OCR of that table is corrupted, so clean p.390 narrative quoted instead. Paper states0.0001 is lowest calculated combined p; no smaller p inferred. Completion source review (n_r): The liking analysis constructs in-name and not-in-name average probabilities for each of the explicitly stated 26 English letters, and Table 3 includes A–Z. Thus 26 letter-level observations are the analytic units for the liking t-test; participant recruitment is a separate role. Not derived from df or participant table-cell sums.
